findings.summary: The resume turn re-adopts the pre-suspension coordinator run instead of invoking the model with the injected decision. decision_interrupt calls deps.coordinator.turn on the same round_no that blocked; AgentRunCoordinator derives run_id = derive_run_id(thread_id, f"coordinator-{round_no}", 1) from a thread_id that is stable across the suspension, and that round's run already wrote a succeeded result.json. The attempt loop only skips a *failed* prior (adapters.py:112), so it breaks at attempt 1; AgentRunLauncher.launch sees find_result(session_root) is not None and returns an adopted ticket without spawning (agent_run.py:303-305); wait/poll replays the same result and parse_envelope yields the old blocked + waiting_on=decision verdict with no acknowledged_message_id. Required behavior 3 -- persist the DecisionInput in the resumed envelope before invoking the coordinator, and the coordinator structured result must acknowledge message_id -- is therefore unreachable in production: N7 rejects the round, round_no advances, and round 2 runs through coordinator_turn, whose envelope carries no decision. record_turn_result then persists the stale blocked result, so any later re-entry re-adopts it permanently. No test or acceptance scenario catches this because every drill substitutes a fake coordinator for the real AgentRunCoordinator/AgentRunLauncher pair.

Two independent question notes are published for one human-decision wait, and only one of them can resume the interrupt. On suspension the line asks via LineInterruptPort.ask (card idempotency_key 'e2-card:<folder>', question key 'e2-question:<folder>:<gen>:<round>') and also writes the legacy blocked+waiting_on=decision terminal; the scheduler then establishes the park and escalates, publishing its own card ('goal-line-card:<folder>') and its own question note ('parked:<folder>:<run_id>') into stall-state board_question_note_id. GoalInterruptBridge only walks the decision chain for interrupt['question_note_id'], i.e. the E2 note, so a human answering the scheduler's escalation question -- the note operators have always answered and the only one E1's DecisionBridge tracks for a non-legacy owner -- resolves to the parked owner and wakes the line, which re-enters decision_interrupt, finds no resume receipt, and simply re-suspends. The verdict is silently discarded rather than resuming the generation.

Two verification facts recorded rather than asserted. This reviewer has file inspection only and no shell, so the prescribed `git diff --exit-code f0c4c951 93c062a1 -- . ':(exclude).dev-dispatch'` was not executed and tree equality between the two SHAs is unverified; the .dev-dispatch/ namespace as inspected contains only metadata, consistent with a compliant metadata-only materialization. Separately, the committed implement handoff records work_head_commit 2d3b2c40c0edaffa11a00bff7d95efebd66432b0 while the dispatch context names f0c4c951e2c3d7cfef72c1c139c97b0283e07b21 as the product commit -- the same mismatch shape the attempt-1 and attempt-2 final reviews recorded.
